proposal: The Mandate recommends that, right after inauguration, the President task the NSC's Senior Director for Intelligence Programs with a 60-day review of current covert action findings and of possible new ones, independent of the responsible agencies, and with identification of which agencies are best equipped. status_summary: No public record of the Mandate's 60-day review of existing covert action findings by the NSC Senior Director for Intelligence Programs, of an assessment of which agencies are best equipped, or of DOD capabilities being placed under covert action findings was found. Press reports describe new covert action instead: on 2025-10-15 the President publicly confirmed authorizing CIA covert action in Venezuela, which anonymous US officials told the New York Times was set out in a classified presidential finding, and a CNN report republished 2026-05-12, relying mostly on anonymous sources, described an expanded CIA campaign against cartels in Mexico after the President formally updated and expanded the agency's authorities. The Mandate contemplates new findings as a possible outcome of its review, so these reports are related context rather than evidence that the review took place. Because covert action is classified, this assessment rests on press reporting.

timeline.event: Reporting by the New York Times, carried by the Boston Globe, said the administration had secretly authorized the CIA to conduct covert action in Venezuela under a classified presidential finding, citing anonymous officials; the President publicly confirmed that he had authorized it.

CNN reported, mostly from anonymous sources, an expanded CIA campaign against cartels in Mexico following a formal update and expansion of the agency's authorities; the CIA declined to comment and Mexico's president said she was not told in advance of one operation.

title: Review all covert action findings in 60 days and use DOD capabilities in support
uncertainties: Stage is not_started because none of the Mandate's specific steps (the independent 60-day review, the agency assessment, DOD capabilities under findings, staffing) is publicly documented; new findings reported in the press are shown as parallel context. A review could have occurred without public notice, so this rests on absence of evidence. Both sources rely on anonymous officials, except the President's public confirmation about Venezuela. The CNN article body does not give the month of the authorities update; a linked earlier CNN story is dated October 2025, which is why that month was used in the earlier draft; it is not relied on here. The NSC reorganization is covered in c02-03, and CIA briefings on existing findings in c07-04's chapter pages.
